bug_description.original:
Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5073877744877568

Project: mongoose
Fuzzing Engine: libFuzzer
Fuzz Target: fuzz
Job Type: libfuzzer_ubsan_mongoose
Platform Id: linux

Crash Type: UNKNOWN READ
Crash Address: 0x78fabd5cb000
Crash State:
  deliver_chunked_chunks
  http_cb
  fuzz.c
  
Sanitizer: undefined (UBSAN)

Recommended Security Severity: Medium
bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 62609: mongoose HTTP chunked transfer encoding parser accepts non-hex characters in the chunk size prefix. The getchunk() function scans the prefix stopping only at CR/LF, then feeds all scanned bytes (including non-hex characters) to mg_unhexn(). Non-hex characters produce nibble values exceeding 4 bits via mg_unhex_nimble(), and the accumulated chunk size overflows unsigned 64-bit arithmetic. The boundary check i+n+4 wraps to a small value, bypassing the guard. The inflated chunk size is used as a memmove length in deliver_chunked_chunks(), causing an out-of-bounds read (SEGV). The fix restricts the prefix scan to valid hex digits only via is_hex_digit().

source.description: The chunk prefix scanning loop accepts any byte that is not CR or LF, including non-hex characters. This consumes attacker-controlled bytes from the HTTP chunked body into the prefix length i, which determines how many characters are interpreted as the hex chunk size.
source.value_from: The fuzzer harness copies PoC bytes into c->recv via mg_iobuf_add (test/fuzz.c:111), then triggers http_cb which parses HTTP headers and dispatches to deliver_chunked_chunks for chunked requests. getchunk receives the chunk body as struct mg_str s from deliver_chunked_chunks; value `s.ptr[0..i-1]`; from `while (i < s.len && s.ptr[i] != '\r' && s.ptr[i] != '\n') i++;`

sink.description: memmove uses the inflated chunk data length dl (equal to n from getchunk) as the byte count. Since n is near SIZE_MAX, this reads far beyond the allocated receive buffer, causing a SEGV.

root_cause.description: The boundary check s.len < i + n + 4 is intended to verify the chunk fits in the buffer. When n is near SIZE_MAX (due to non-hex characters producing overflowed nibble accumulation), the addition i + n + 4 wraps to a small value via unsigned 64-bit overflow, causing the check to pass despite n being astronomical.

tainted_value_origin.description: Attacker-controlled HTTP chunk prefix bytes, including non-hex characters such as 'U' (0x55), are scanned past by the prefix loop, inflating i to include bytes that mg_unhexn will misinterpret.

coarse_trace.summary: Parses the HTTP request from the receive buffer, detects Transfer-Encoding: chunked, and dispatches to deliver_chunked_chunks.

Scans the chunk size prefix accepting non-hex characters, converts them via mg_unhexn producing an overflowed chunk length, and the boundary check passes due to integer overflow in the guard expression.
Uses the overflowed chunk length as the byte count for memmove, reading far past the receive buffer boundary and triggering a SEGV.

fine_trace.note: Scans the chunk size prefix from attacker-controlled HTTP body. The loop condition accepts any byte except CR (0x0D) and LF (0x0A), so non-hex characters like 'U' (0x55), 'o', 'C', etc. in the PoC are included. After scanning, i equals the total prefix length including all non-hex bytes. The fix replaces this condition with is_hex_digit(s.ptr[i]), stopping at the first non-hex character.

Converts the first i bytes of the chunk prefix to an unsigned long chunk size. Internally, mg_unhexn (src/str.c:179) calls mg_unhex_nimble for each byte, which maps non-hex characters via (c - 'W'). For 'U' (0x55), this yields 0x55 - 0x57 = 0xFE as an unsigned char (254). Since the nibble value exceeds 4 bits, the OR in v |= nibble bleeds into higher bit positions. After enough iterations with high-nibble characters, n approaches SIZE_MAX (e.g., 16 'U' characters yield n = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF).

Boundary check intended to verify the chunk data plus framing fits in the buffer. With n near SIZE_MAX, the unsigned addition i + n + 4 overflows 64-bit arithmetic, wrapping to a small value (e.g., i + SIZE_MAX + 4 mod 2^64 = i + 3). The check therefore evaluates as s.len < (small value), which is false for any reasonably sized buffer, so execution continues. The subsequent framing checks at lines 965-966 (s.ptr[i]=CR, s.ptr[i+1]=LF, and s.ptr[i+n+2]=CR, s.ptr[i+n+3]=LF) also use overflowed index expressions that wrap back to positions near i, matching the actual CR/LF bytes placed there by the PoC.
Outputs the overflowed chunk size n to the caller via the datalen out-parameter. The value is near SIZE_MAX.

fine_trace.code: memmove(p + processed, buf + ofs + pl, dl);
fine_trace.note: dl equals the overflowed n from getchunk. memmove reads dl bytes (near SIZE_MAX) starting from buf + ofs + pl, which is within the receive buffer, but the read extends far beyond any allocated memory. The resulting SEGV is reported by UBSan as UNKNOWN READ at a high address.

format.name: HTTP request with chunked Transfer-Encoding containing non-hex chunk prefix
format.contract: The PoC must be a valid HTTP request with Transfer-Encoding: chunked header and a chunk body whose size prefix contains non-hex, non-CR/LF bytes (such as 'U' = 0x55) that cause mg_unhexn to produce an overflowed chunk length near SIZE_MAX, so that getchunk's boundary check is bypassed via unsigned integer overflow and deliver_chunked_chunks performs an out-of-bounds memmove read.

parser_admitted.description: The HTTP request is parsed successfully by mg_http_parse and the Transfer-Encoding header is detected as 'chunked' by mg_is_chunked, dispatching to deliver_chunked_chunks.
